topic: Simon the cat, the only animal ever awarded Britain's Dickin Medal, and his death in UK quarantine after the 1949 Yangtze Incident
title: The Only Cat Ever Awarded Britain's War Medal
description: AI-narrated commentary on a real, independently-documented piece of naval history: Simon, the HMS Amethyst ship's cat who survived the 1949 Yangtze Incident and became the only cat ever awarded the Dickin Medal, Britain's top honor for animal bravery in war.

hook_candidates.text: A cat once earned a British war medal, survived a direct hit, and that wasn't his worst day.
What does it actually take for an animal to earn Britain's highest bravery medal in wartime?
Everyone assumes the shelling was the worst part of this war cat's story. It wasn't.
In 1949 a British warship sat trapped on a Chinese river for months, and its most decorated survivor was a cat.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who insists military medals are only for human soldiers because they want to show a wounded ship's cat once earned one too.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume the direct hit and the shelling were the worst thing that happened to this decorated war cat.
closing_comment: Simon really is the only cat ever awarded Britain's war medal, and his citation plus the fan-mail 'cat officer' post are both on public record.

sources.note: Official awarding body confirms Simon is the only cat ever to receive the Dickin Medal.
Confirms the 1949 shelling wound, the weeks-long Yangtze siege, and his death in UK quarantine on Nov 28, 1949.
